prompt: In the book, using the LeanFM server, take screenshots that show actual usage scenarios.
question: What does a real session look like for players, the creator and a watcher?
event_source: the running GoServer application driven by scripted people in headless Chrome
reducer: named DevTools screenshots after each scripted step
boundary: local loopback app on port 8095; in-memory state discarded afterwards; no credentials shown

captures.title: Welcome
captures.caption: A visitor chooses a local display name. Nothing else is needed for the local preview.
steps: open the app

captures.title: Creating a challenge
captures.caption: Alice is in the lobby and fills in a challenge: a 9×9 board, three players, and a byo-yomi clock of one minute of main time and then three periods of ten seconds, the same for people and bots. The ko rule stays on Auto, which is off for three players.
steps: sign in as alice
fill in the New challenge form

captures.title: Planning seats
captures.caption: Before the start the creator decides, seat by seat, whether a person or a bot plays and which team the seat is on. Alice took seat 1, bob sat in seat 2, and alice marked seat 3 as a bot.
steps: alice: create the challenge (seated automatically)
alice: set seat 3 to Bot
bob: open the challenge, Sit here

captures.title: Aiming a stone
captures.caption: On her turn alice moves the pointer over the board: a translucent stone in her colour shows exactly where a click will play. Over an occupied point, a point the ko rule forbids, or when it is not her turn, there is no preview and the pointer shows that a click would be refused. Above the tabs, the play bar keeps whose turn it is and the clock in view.
steps: alice: move the pointer over an empty point on her turn

captures.title: Reading the bot’s search
captures.caption: Alice steps back one move, to the position where the bot searched for its last move. The panel lists the moves that search weighed, with visit share and expected reward; the blue discs on the board are the same search as a heat map. Proj. and Outlook give every seat’s projected final score and expected reward, and the timeline under them plots the projections move by move.
steps: alice and bob alternate stones by clicking the board; the bot answers each round
alice: Back one move

captures.title: A watcher explores a variation
captures.caption: Carol is watching, not playing. She steps back to move 3, tries a different stone (the gold ring marks a variation), and asks for a local search. The analysis runs in her browser only: the dashed branch in the tree never reaches the server, and the live game continues.
steps: carol: open the challenge as a watcher
carol: Home, then Forward three times
carol: click an empty point
carol: Analyze here

captures.title: Proposing a team merge
captures.caption: During play bob proposes merging his team with alice’s. The Seats tab flags a proposal waiting for her answer; there the proposal shows who has accepted and who is still to answer; it takes effect only when every person on both teams accepts, and it is permanent.
steps: bob: Merge my team with Team 1, Propose

captures.title: Playing as a team, on autopilot
captures.caption: After the merge the score table shows alice and bob as team 1 with a combined total. Alice then lets a bot play her seat; the seat, team and name stay hers, and the bot’s move publishes its search like any other bot move. She can take the seat back at any time.
steps: alice: Accept merge
alice: Let a bot play for me

captures.title: The result
captures.caption: When every remaining player has passed in a row the game ends. The Chat tab lights up with an unread count; the server announces team scores and the winners in the game conversation. Everyone, players included, can now branch and analyse any position.
steps: alice passes with the P key, bob with the Pass button, until the bot also passes

captures.title: Reviewing together
captures.caption: After the game alice steps back to move 2, passes for the seat to move there and lets the computer pick the next move. Both moves are kept on the server for everyone in the game, and her remark is pinned to the position she was looking at: the Chat tab shows the remarks along the line on the board, so stepping back hides it again and anyone who walks into this variation sees it.
steps: alice: Home, then → twice
alice: P, then C
alice: write a remark in Chat

captures.title: Rooms and games as tabs
captures.caption: Every room alice has open is a tab along the top, with + Rooms for finding and creating rooms; inside a room, the Lobby (its conversation and challenge list) comes first and every open game has its own tab. Tabs stay alive in the background: a game keeps its variations and analysis, and a tab shows a badge when a move or a merge waits for her or messages arrive. Responses only ever land in the tab that asked for them.
steps: alice: + Rooms, create Post-game
alice: back to the lobby room tab

note: Bot moves come from a time-limited search, so stone positions differ between runs; the scenario steps do not.
